items.titleEn: Here's why SentinelOne, Okta, Zscaler, and Crowdstrike stocks rising today
items.summaryEn: Buy PANW. The earnings signal is unusually strong: +39% revenue, +35% remaining performance obligations to $21B, and 26% growth guidance. Management is also leaning into AI security (Applied Compute acquisition) which keeps the market paying up for the “AI defense” leaders. This should pull the whole group higher into early-December earnings. Key Risk: Guidance or billings disappoint next quarter, breaking the “spending is accelerating” narrative. Buy CRWD. If PANW’s results confirm broad enterprise security demand, CRWD tends to benefit disproportionately because investors treat it as a top-tier platform for stopping modern attacks. The article’s setup (sector tone + AI threat focus) points to another earnings beat cycle for CRWD in the first week of December.

items.titleEn: Anthropic IPO opens the door: 4 tech companies that may go public
items.summaryEn: Buy ANT on strength. The article says the IPO already raised $80B and ANT is up 20% in the grey market—momentum can carry into the first days as investors chase AI IPO liquidity even in a bear AI tape. Key catalyst is continued “IPO door opening” sentiment that keeps demand high for the next AI listing wave. Key Risk: Grey-market/IPO hype fades fast after pricing and early trading, and the stock sells off with the broader AI complex. Buy MSFT. If OpenAI follows Anthropic’s playbook, it likely raises more capital and accelerates product rollout—benefiting Microsoft as OpenAI’s core partner (cloud + distribution). This is a cleaner way to own the OpenAI upside without waiting for an IPO.

items.titleEn: OpenAI faces fresh legal trouble as Arizona opens criminal probe over rogue agents
items.summaryEn: Buy CrowdStrike (CRWD) or Palo Alto Networks (PANW). If banks and enterprises tighten controls on autonomous agents, budgets shift to detection, incident response, and identity/access monitoring. The news increases demand for tools that catch unusual agent behavior and stop lateral movement into financial systems. Key Risk: Regulators focus on OpenAI-specific remedies without broad enterprise spending increases on security tooling. Short Microsoft (MSFT) or sell MSFT call spreads tied to OpenAI exposure. The Arizona criminal probe plus California’s lawsuit signal escalating legal risk around “rogue agents” and bank access—exactly the kind of event that drives regulators to demand costly safety changes and can trigger revenue/usage limits. Legal overhang also pressures valuation multiples for AI platform winners.

items.titleEn: Why are Nvidia, AMD, Intel stocks surging in premarket trading today?
items.summaryEn: Buy Nvidia (NVDA). The article flags a clean demand signal: data-center revenue up 110% and guidance for Q4 sales ~$130B (+/-3%) ahead of expectations, implying customers didn’t pause spending even amid leadership uncertainty. Anthropic’s IPO hype is the catalyst, but NVDA’s earnings/guidance are the fuel. Key Risk: A sharp AI capex slowdown shows up in the next quarter, forcing NVDA to cut guidance despite today’s enthusiasm. Buy AMD (AMD). The setup is stronger than a generic AI bounce: data-center revenue +97% and Q4 revenue expected to accelerate to ~$17B, plus Helios-linked demand from Anthropic ecosystem. The Taalas acquisition supports more efficient inference—helping AMD convert AI interest into recurring, higher-margin orders.

items.titleEn: Anthropic to begin trading after record-breaking market debut tops SpaceX record
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Anthropic will begin trading on Thursday on the Nasdaq exchange after pricing its initial public offering at $83 a share, above its expected range and toppling SpaceX's IPO to set a new record. Hot demand for the AI giant brushed aside market jitters over the spy scandal that toppled Nvidia's chief executive, despite lingering concerns about an investment bubble.

items.titleEn: Column: Why Anthropic's IPO may not be enough to restore AI investor confidence
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA on weakness after the earnings beat and raised FY2028 revenue growth (75% vs 70%). The market sold off anyway, but the guidance signal is the clearest “AI capex still accelerating” proof. If NVDA stabilizes, it should pull the whole AI chip complex higher (neoclouds/hyperscalers follow). Key Risk: Jensen’s exit plus ongoing China-spying allegations trigger a credibility hit that leads customers to pause AI infrastructure orders despite strong guidance. Sell AI-exposed software/infra laggards (e.g., Palantir (PLTR) and other unprofitable AI beneficiaries) that rally on NVDA headlines but lack durable demand proof. If the AI trade keeps de-risking after the Anthropic IPO hype, money rotates back to the highest-conviction cash generators—chips and picks-and-shovels—leaving weaker names to bleed.

items.titleEn: Did Trump discuss Jensen Huang controversy with Xi? Here's what he said
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. Trump’s brief mention of Huang and lack of “spy” confirmation reduces immediate political tail risk, while the bigger driver is the new US export rules already forcing a China pause. That creates a near-term earnings overhang that the market can over-discount; NVDA’s core AI demand outside China stays intact and guidance can stabilize as licensed/non-China channels absorb demand. Key Risk: A further escalation of US-China chip controls that permanently shrinks NVDA’s China revenue and forces deeper margin cuts. Buy ASML. If the US tightens and China retaliates, China will try to accelerate domestic semiconductor capacity, but it can’t quickly replace leading-edge lithography. ASML’s installed base and service/upgrade cycle benefit while competitors face slower substitution. The Huang/Trump noise is a catalyst for “supply-chain durability” re-rating toward the picks-and-shovels.

items.titleEn: Who is Rene Haas? The former Nvidia insider who could replace Jensen Huang
items.summaryEn: Buy Nvidia (NVDA). The article signals a credible internal-adjacent successor profile: Haas has deep semiconductor/AI platform knowledge (Arm tech in Grace/Vera) and long experience managing Nvidia’s culture and relationships. Even with the stock down on uncertainty, fundamentals are still surging (massive revenue growth and strong forward forecast). Key Risk: Nvidia’s board picks a leader who can’t maintain Huang’s execution style, causing AI product roadmap delays and customer confidence to drop. Sell Arm (ARM). Haas is a contender, but the process raises a direct overhang: if he leaves or splits focus between Arm and SoftBank, Arm’s AI push (licensing + finished silicon) could slow. The market will discount Arm’s growth multiple on leadership uncertainty and potential conflicts with Nvidia ties.

items.titleEn: Is TTWO a good stock to buy as GTA 6 launches?
items.summaryEn: Buy Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ: TTWO). Early reviews are strong (Metacritic 99) and Wall Street is already lifting GTA 6 sales and net bookings expectations (Wells Fargo: ~65M copies FY27; net bookings $9.76B). The upside case is not just the box office—it’s converting launch demand into GTA 6 recurring spend via online + future platform releases, similar to GTA Online’s long tail. Key risk: GTA 6 sales or online monetization come in below the now-hyped forecasts, so the stock sells off even after a great launch. Key Risk: GTA 6 fails to beat the already-raised Wall Street expectations for sales and recurring online revenue. Sell/short TTWO for a near-term fade. The stock already jumped ~6% into launch and the market may have priced the “record-breaking” narrative. If the first official sales numbers and guidance don’t immediately confirm the most bullish revisions, the stock can retrace because investors bought the story before the data. Key risk: Sales and guidance beat hard on the first prints, triggering momentum buying and forcing shorts to cover.

items.titleEn: Nvidia stock under pressure as Colette Kress makes her first big move
items.summaryEn: Buy NASDAQ:NVDA. The news is negative on sentiment, but the fundamentals are intact: record revenue ($115.8B), data-center growth (+110%), and a strong Q4 guide (~$130B). Accelerating pay reviews is a retention move that reduces the risk of talent flight during the CEO transition, supporting execution on the Vera Rubin roadmap and customer relationships. Key Risk: The board fails to quickly install credible leadership, causing engineers and key partners to lose confidence and execution to slip. Sell short/underweight the most levered AI infrastructure names that depend on cheap financing (e.g., CrowdStrike?—no; instead target high-burn AI hardware/software peers). The second-order read: if NVDA’s leadership uncertainty keeps the stock volatile, capital rotates away from riskier, cash-burning AI plays toward the “picks-and-shovels” winner (NVDA).

items.titleEn: Anthropic's $81 billion IPO eclipses SpaceX, but can its valuation hold?
items.summaryEn: Buy ANT on the first day/first pullback. The IPO priced above the range on huge demand, and the company is scaling revenue fast (annualised run rate ~$81B; first 9 months sales $33.24B). The market is paying for frontier AI exposure that’s hard to access otherwise, and the $26B private placement supports continued funding and momentum. Thesis killer: computing costs stay structurally higher than revenue growth, so margins don’t improve and the $1.5T valuation compresses quickly. Key Risk: Margins fail to improve because AI infrastructure costs keep rising faster than revenue. Buy NVDA as the second-order beneficiary. Anthropic’s massive multiyear compute commitments (hundreds of billions through 2045) imply sustained demand for AI chips, networking, and data-center buildouts—especially from the leading supplier ecosystem. Even if Anthropic’s profitability is debated, the capex cycle still flows through NVDA’s platform. Thesis killer: AI capex slows or shifts to cheaper/alternative hardware that reduces NVDA’s share of spend.

items.titleEn: Samsung and SK Hynix stocks fall again as Nvidia earnings boost fades
items.summaryEn: Buy. Nvidia’s earnings didn’t “cure” AI anxiety, so memory names sold off on fading momentum, not collapsing fundamentals. Samsung is still levered to elevated server DRAM/HBM pricing, and the foreign outflow is the immediate pressure point. If AI capex spending holds, margins should remain supported longer than the market is pricing. Key Risk: AI data-center spending slows enough to force DRAM/HBM price declines and margin compression. Buy. The stock reversed gains after Nvidia fell, but SK Hynix’s demand backdrop (server DRAM and high-bandwidth memory) is the same driver that initially lifted the sector. The selloff looks like positioning unwinds plus valuation anxiety; a stabilization in foreign flows can trigger a fast rebound.

items.titleEn: Lenovo Group stock analysis after earnings: is this Dell rival a buy or sell?
items.summaryEn: Buy Dell. The article flags Dell down ~46% from its peak and at the lowest level since late May—classic oversold behavior in a sector that’s already de-risked. If Lenovo’s AI-driven infrastructure pipeline is real, hyperscalers and data centers still need supply; Dell should benefit from the same capex cycle while starting from a much cheaper valuation after the selloff. This is a mean-reversion + AI infrastructure demand bet, not a “story” bet. Key Risk: Enterprise/AI infrastructure spending slows materially, forcing further earnings cuts and keeping Dell’s multiple compressed. Sell Lenovo Group. Despite strong revenue growth (AI +79% YoY), the stock is in a clear technical downtrend: below the 61.8% retracement, under the 50/200-day EMAs, and a death-cross is likely—so rallies get sold. The market is also punishing AI-exposed hardware names together, and Lenovo’s quarter included a large loss tied to derivative fair-value moves, which keeps sentiment fragile. Key upside is a bounce to ~$20, but the near-term setup favors downside toward ~$14.78 then ~$10.
